The Feasts of the Most High

precepts.text: The Lord appointed a set time, and on the morrow all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel not one died. He touches the nations but spares His people.
precepts.point: When it says the remainder of wrath He shall restrain, it means He is not going to destroy everything and everybody like He did in the flood, where even then eight remained. When the Lord touches up on something, He touches up on him.

note.label: Psalm 76: God Is Known in Judah and Terrible to the Kings of the Earth

precepts.why:
“Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: the remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain.” When we see the Lord put in his judgment upon the earth, everybody will know that the Most High did it. And the remainder of wrath he shall restrain means he is not going to destroy everything and everybody like he did in the flood, where even then eight remained.

Egypt shows how he does it. “And the Lord appointed a set time, saying, To morrow the Lord shall do this thing in the land. And the Lord did that thing on the morrow, and all the cattle of Egypt died: but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one.”

He appointed a set time, and on the morrow all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel not one died. He touches the nations but spares his people. When the Lord touches up on something, he touches up on him. That is the wrath that praises him and the remainder that is restrained.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why: One of the plagues. “Behold, to morrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as hath not been in Egypt since the foundation thereof even until now.” That goes with Revelation 8:7, where it talks about hail and fire mingled with blood. This confirms that America is spiritual Egypt: the third part of the sea became blood goes back to Egypt being plagued with the water turned to blood, for the sake of our young babies being thrown in the water to the alligators; the fish died in Egypt as well; and Egypt was dark for three days, Exodus 10:22, as the third part of the sun, moon and stars are darkened. It is repeating the same plagues over and over again, but on a technological level. The Lord had it done on a natural level through Moses, darkening the moon and stars, water turned to blood; these are technological plagues causing the same exact plagues again on a technological scale, nuclear warfare, fire, satellites falling. It is the same thing. And where was Israel? We were fine; them plagues didn't come near us, we were in the land, we were good. So in Revelation 8 we are in the wilderness; while they are suffering over here, we are good, all over again. We ain't going to experience none of that.

points: All the cattle of Egypt died: but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one. Killing the cattle of Egypt caused what? Famine.

note.label: The Plagues Coming to America

points: The Lord sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt. The hail smote every herb of the field, and brake every tree of the field, and every man and beast that was in the field. Hail fire from the sky came down on ancient Egypt. Guess what: he is going to do that again today, but them hails on modern day Egypt are going to be nuclear bombs.

note.label: The Plagues Coming to America

points: A grievous murrain fell upon the cattle of Egypt, upon the horses, asses, camels, oxen, and sheep; and with this fifth plague the Most High was mocking Hathor, the Egyptian idol goddess of cattle.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Picture what was taking place in the land: flies all over Egypt, but where Israel dwelt there were no flies; the water was blood, but where Israel dwelt the water was good; the cattle of Egypt died, but Israel's cattle lived. The plagues touched Pharaoh, his servants, and the Egyptians only; they did not touch the Israelites at all, because this was the Lord redeeming the Israelites.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: The Lord severed between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: all the cattle of Egypt died, but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one. Pharaoh sent, and behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead; and his heart was hardened.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Moses sprinkled ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast throughout all the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians themselves and upon all the Egyptians. With this sixth plague the Most High was mocking Sekhmet, the Egyptian idol goddess of health and beauty.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Some mock and ask, What type of God says let my people go and then keeps hardening Pharaoh's heart so he will not let them go? That is exactly the God we serve, and the Lord tells you Himself why He did it: for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: The same thing is happening now, right here in this captivity. The powers of Babylon know what is being taught, yet the Lord hardens their hearts so that they keep passing laws and pressing against His people, so that the Most High can show His power again, just as He did in Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Before the hail the Lord gave warning: gather thy cattle and all that thou hast in the field, for upon every man and beast found in the field the hail shall come down, and they shall die.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses; they began to recognize the God of heaven and earth, the God of the Israelites.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: He that regarded not the word of the Lord left his servants and his cattle in the field. Many in Egypt held certain idols in more favor than others, and these trusted that Nut, the idol goddess of the sky, would keep them safe.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: With this seventh plague the Most High was mocking Nut and Geb, the Egyptian idol gods of the sky and the earth, striking from the sky and burning along the ground they were supposed to rule.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: This was no regular hail. There was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation; the fire ran along upon the ground.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. The Lord does not play; our God is a terrible God.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Pharaoh said, I have sinned this time: the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked. This time? So all the other times, none of that was sin? Only now, under the thunder and hail, does he see it.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Moses answered that the thunder and hail would cease, that thou mayest know how that the earth is the Lord's; but as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the Lord God.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: The flax and the barley were smitten, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was bolled; but the wheat and the rie were not smitten, for they were not grown up.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more and hardened his heart, he and his servants. He still had the wheat and the rie in the ground, because they were not grown up yet, and that is part of why he went right back to hardening himself.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart
